text:
A Study on a Large-Model-Based Intelligent
Question-Answering System for the
Overhead Contact System Field

Junkai Huang  |  Student ID: 2023115799
Supervisor: Prof. Deqing Huang
Undergraduate Project Proposal Defense  |  Electronic and Electrical Engineering
notes: Good morning. I am Junkai Huang. My project studies an intelligent question-answering system for Chinese overhead contact system standards. The central aim is to make answers traceable to the correct document edition and supporting clause. I will introduce the research questions, the planned method, and the evaluation design. This is a proposal presentation: performance targets and future experiments are not completed results.

The presentation has four parts. First, I will explain why standards-based question answering needs more than a fluent response. Second, I will define the three research questions. Third, I will describe the retrieval, edition and evidence checks, followed by the controlled evaluation. Finally, I will discuss the available evidence, remaining risks and project schedule.

text: Why standards-based QA needs traceable evidence
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Reliable answers preserve the clause, edition and conditions
Focus: permitted Chinese PDF/DOCX standards; consultation and study
notes: The research object is technical information in documents, rather than the physical operation of railway equipment. These standards contain specialised terms, numerical limits, units and edition-dependent conditions. Exact-term matching may miss a paraphrase; semantic matching may retrieve a similar clause from the wrong edition. Even a relevant passage may not support the requested conclusion. The three branches in this conceptual figure define the three questions I will test. The output is intended for study and consultation, not engineering approval.

text: Related research informs three testable choices
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Ground generation in documents; preserve exact terms
Existing tools and APIs; no model training
Test paraphrase matching and follow-up context
Hybrid is a hypothesis; follow-ups use rules
Check relevance; assess retrieval and answers separately
Human semantic scoring; no LLM judge
Consider Chinese retrieval and evidence use
Corpus-specific performance remains to be tested
Project gap: test these methods under edition-dependent technical queries
notes: RAG motivates grounding a model answer in retrieved documents. BM25 provides an interpretable lexical baseline, while dense retrieval provides semantic matching. These are complementary mechanisms, but improvement from combining them must be measured. Query-rewriting work motivates limited rules for follow-ups; I will not train a rewriter. Distractor studies motivate checking evidence relevance, and RAGAs motivates separating retrieval from answer assessment. This project uses human semantic scoring rather than an LLM judge. None of the cited studies establishes performance on this railway corpus.

text: Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Does Hybrid improve evidence recall over BM25 and Dense?
Does edition filtering reduce answers using a non-requested edition?
Does the Evidence Gate reduce unsupported answers without excessive refusal?
Aim: evidence-based question answering for overhead contact system standards
notes: My aim is to develop and evaluate evidence-based question answering for these standards. RQ1 tests whether hybrid retrieval improves recall compared with lexical and dense retrieval separately. RQ2 tests whether edition filtering reduces the use of non-requested editions. RQ3 tests whether an Evidence Gate reduces unsupported answers without causing excessive refusal. The intended contribution is a curated, traceable corpus and benchmark, together with controlled comparisons and failure analysis. I am not claiming a new foundation model or an established performance improvement.

text: Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study

20-30 permitted documents
Parsing, chunks and SQLite
PDF file-page or DOCX paragraph/table location
notes: The planned system separates local document retrieval from online generation. Permitted PDFs and DOCX files will be extracted, chunked and indexed with their standard identifiers, years, hashes and source locations in SQLite. The question and any rule-based follow-up determine the eligible passages. Retrieval is followed by the Evidence Gate. Accepted evidence goes to DeepSeek, with citation and excerpt checks; insufficient evidence leads to refusal or clarification. Streamlit presents the answer and traceable sources. Only text with appropriate permission may leave the device.

text: Hybrid retrieval: lexical and semantic matching
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Lexical matching for identifiers and specialised terms
Cosine similarity for questions using different wording
Consistent Chinese segmentation and a small domain dictionary
Hybrid score = (1 - w) B + w D
B, D: min-max normalised BM25 and cosine scores
w in {0.25, 0.50, 0.75}; select on development data only
Top-K = 5  |  Freeze preprocessing, chunks, models and settings
notes: All retrieval methods will use consistent Chinese tokenisation and the same eligible chunks. Identifiers, terms, numbers and units must be preserved. For each question, BM25 and cosine scores are min-max normalised over the eligible chunks. The hybrid score combines the normalised lexical score B and dense score D. I will choose the weight from three candidates using development Recall at five, then MRR at five, with ties favouring 0.50. Corpus, preprocessing and parameters will be frozen before testing. This slide describes the proposed method, not a tuned implementation.
/01_Proposal_Draft_EN.md Reproducible method: constant positive scores map to 1; other constants to 0; ties favour w=0.50

text: Edition handling prevents silent year substitution
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
A copy is not a new edition
A1 disables edition checks but retains standard-family filtering
notes: Edition identity is separate from relevance. If a question specifies an available edition, retrieval should use that edition. If the requested edition is missing, the system must refuse rather than silently use another year. Ambiguity requires clarification. Duplicate copies do not count as separate formal editions. The target is two standard families with two usable editions each, but availability and permissions remain to be confirmed. To isolate edition handling, ablation A1 retains family filtering while disabling year restrictions and edition availability or ambiguity checks.

text: The Evidence Gate screens for insufficient context
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Accept if: lexical coverage >= threshold OR raw cosine >= threshold
Distinct content-token overlap; exclude identifiers and fixed stopwords
Metadata, citation identifiers and literal excerpt matching
Required facts, numerical values, units and applicable conditions
notes: The gate uses two signals: lexical coverage and raw cosine similarity. Coverage is the matched distinct query content tokens divided by all distinct query content tokens, excluding standard identifiers and fixed stopwords. The same segmenter is used for passages; an empty content-token set scores zero. Thresholds are selected on development data. The gate accepts when either signal reaches its threshold. Automatic checks validate metadata, citation identifiers and literal excerpts. Human scoring still determines semantic support, including values, units and conditions. High similarity alone does not prove correctness.

text: A fixed benchmark separates tuning from testing
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Required facts, units, conditions, edition and evidence locations
Keep related facts/dialogues together; no test-based tuning
notes: The planned benchmark contains one hundred manually checked questions. Twenty are for development, including sixteen answerable items. Eighty are held out for testing, including sixty-four answerable and sixteen unanswerable items. Each record will include required facts, values, units, conditions, editions and evidence spans. Related facts and dialogues stay in one split to reduce leakage. Only the development set selects weights and gate thresholds. Before the test, I will freeze the corpus, questions, code, prompts, models and configuration. The main experiment then has eighty questions across five configurations: four hundred executions.

text: Five configurations isolate retrieval and safeguards
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
RQ1: B1 / B2 / B3     RQ2: B3 / A1     RQ3: B3 / A2
notes: The five configurations answer the three research questions without introducing extra formal groups. B1, B2 and B3 compare BM25, Dense and Hybrid retrieval. B3 versus A1 isolates edition checks: standard-family filtering remains in place. B3 versus A2 isolates only the retrieval gate: prompts, citation validation and error handling remain active. All five use the same frozen corpus, test questions and generation settings. Each of the four hundred test executions will retain rankings, gate and edition decisions, answers, failures and timing. I will report unfavourable as well as favourable outcomes.

text: Evaluation measures quality and refusal together
Source: SWJTU proposal, Sections 1-4; planned study
Supported cited claims / all cited claims
All unambiguous edition requests; stratify availability
Targets are planning goals. API/format failures are errors; report counts and coverage.
notes: Retrieval metrics use pre-gate rankings on all sixty-four answerable test questions. Correctness counts only fully correct answers; errors and refusals score zero. Citation support is assessed at claim level, with citation coverage reported separately. Wrong-edition rate includes missing-edition cases among all unambiguous edition requests, and will be stratified by availability. Refusal recall uses the sixteen unanswerable items; false refusal uses the sixty-four answerable items. Unsupported-answer incidence uses all eighty test items. The displayed thresholds are planning goals. Counts, paired differences, uncertainty, coverage and failures are needed to interpret them.

/01_Proposal_Draft_EN.md assessment. Clarification is justified only for pre-labelled ambiguous items; zero denominators are N/A. Unsupported-answer incidence is per all 80 test items. Report citation/answer coverage, counts, paired differences, uncertainty and latency.

text: Sources: proposal §4.6; Week 9 evidence, 4 Nov 2026 (historical snapshot)

Three-document BM25 prototype

DeepSeek checks with synthetic evidence

4 Nov snapshot: 503 chunks, 0 vectors

Live embedding access and identity

Dense / Hybrid and formal benchmark

Corpus permissions and usable editions

Existing CPU hardware; only permitted text sent online.
No model training, OCR, agents, hardware work or deployment.
notes: The dated evidence supports a limited feasibility claim. A three-document BM25 prototype exists, and earlier DeepSeek checks used synthetic evidence. The fourth-of-November read-only snapshot contains three documents, five hundred and three chunks and zero vectors. No live embedding request was made in that evidence package. Therefore, embedding access, Dense and Hybrid retrieval, corpus permissions, usable edition pairs and formal evaluation are still pending. The main controls are to resolve access early, retain local retrieval, limit edition conclusions if pairs are unavailable and keep the study within its original scope.

text:
Traceable QA prototype and source-checked benchmark
Controlled comparisons and documented failure analysis
notes: The expected outputs are a traceable question-answering prototype, a curated corpus and source-checked benchmark, and controlled evidence about retrieval, edition filtering and evidence gating. The main conclusion at proposal stage is that these mechanisms need separate measurement: a working interface does not establish accurate answers. I will report limitations and negative results as well as improvements. Thank you for listening. I welcome questions about the scope, edition handling, evaluation design and feasibility.
